body:
### Describe the bug

I hit this in a production system on Windows: a string constant defined in a .pyx file came out truncated at 2**16 characters after building the extension, with a completely clean build log. It affects both `"..."` and `b"..."` literals. The same code works fine on Linux (gcc), which is why it took me a while to track down.

After digging in, the root cause turned out to be MSVC, not the generated code — cl.exe silently emits only `len mod 65536` bytes of a string literal's initializer data when the (concatenated) literal is longer than 65535 bytes. No error, no warning, even at /W3. But since Cython already splits long literals into 2000-char pieces to work around another MSVC limit (`StringEncoding.split_string_literal`), I think Cython is the right place to also work around this one — or at least fail loudly instead of shipping corrupted constants.

I searched the tracker for similar issues; the closest are #4924 (link.exe hangs with many constants) and #5290 (big integer literals fail on MSVC), but neither covers this. I also checked current master:
`split_string_literal` still only does the 2000-char piece splitting and nothing limits the total literal size, so master generates the same affected code as the 3.0.10 I tested with.

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

```bat
python -c "a='A'*(2**16+3); print(f'a=\"{a}\"\nprint(a)')" > main.pyx
python setup.py build_ext --inplace
python -c "import main"
```

with this setup.py:

```python
from setuptools import setup, Extension
from Cython.Build import cythonize

ext = Extension(name="main", sources=["main.pyx"], language="c++")
setup(ext_modules=cythonize(ext, compiler_directives={'language_level': 3}))
```

Actual output:

```
C:\Users\win10\Desktop\cythonbugtest>python -c "import main"
AAAA
```

Exactly 4 characters, because 65539 chars + 1 NUL terminator = 65540 bytes and 65540 mod 65536 = 4. The build log contains no warning or error at all.

### Expected behaviour

`print(a)` prints all 65539 characters (as it does on Linux with gcc, and as plain CPython does when the same file is executed as a .py module). If the target compiler genuinely can't represent the constant, I'd expect the build to fail with an error rather than produce a silently corrupted extension.

### OS

Windows 10 x64

### Python version

3.11.9 (MSC v.1938, 64 bit)

### Cython version

3.0.10

### Additional context

_No response_

comment_data.body:
For reference the Microsoft link where they describe this is https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-language/maximum-string-length?view=msvc-170. Obviously all compilers have some limits somewhere though so it isn't exclusive to Microsoft (although GCC and clang tend to be a bit bigger I think)

> If the target compiler genuinely can't represent the constant, I'd expect the build to fail with an error rather than produce a silently corrupted extension.

I'd claim that this bit of it *really* should be on Microsoft since it's much easier for them to detect that they've failed than for us to. So please do complain to them! 

I agree that it's probably worth trying to avoid the issue in Cython if there's a sensible way of doing so though.

Additional thoughts: on more recent Cython versions we've changed how strings are loaded. That makes it both better and worse: 
* All the strings are now concatenated into a single C string. That makes it worse because you're more likely to hit the limit. 
* The strings are now compressed (and decompressed to convert them to Python strings). Obviously your example compresses *extremely* well so you're unlikely to hit the issue unless you deliberately turn off compression. But in general it does make it better. 

The general problem remains though.

title: [BUG] str/bytes constants longer than 65535 bytes are silently truncated to len % 2**16 when built with MSVC
